title: Touring with Josephine Baker and Buddy Rich; Mexico City
summary: Edison backed Josephine Baker with Buddy Rich in 1950, then became her musical director in 1952 and spent six months in Mexico City.

story.theme_name: Going abroad: American jazz musicians touring and living in Europe
story.community_name: Going abroad: touring Europe and Japan

blocks.x: Well, when did you go into -- you started to talk about that last time. When did you go into the studios?

Well, 1950, when Josephine Baker first came over to the States. Buddy Rich, we were backing Josephine Baker. He became her musical director. And the band. So from about, oh, about four months we toured with Josephine Baker and then Buddy, you know, it was just theaters. Buddy wanted to play, naturally everybody wanted to play. But Buddy Rich is not the type to be an accompanist, you know. So he split and I became

the trumpet player with her, you know. And then she went back to Paris and came back the next year and I became her musical director. That was in 1952. Oh, I toured with her for a long time. Went to Mexico City six months.
Stayed down there six months, yeah, with Josephine Baker.
You must know Mexico pretty well, then.
Well, Mexico City was all together different than then it is now, you know. But we played at a place called El Patio. It's a night club.
What way was it different then?

Well, you know, now they've got a lot of oil, they're very independent now, you know. But in those days, they depended on the tourists to come through there and a lot of Americans had opened up businesses down there that they were hiring the Mexicans in the businesses. So far as I could see about the political view of it, I don't know.

But, you know, I had a much better time down there in those days than I did this last time, with Sammy Davis, I went down to Acapulco for two weeks with Sammy Davis, with his show. I was playing trumpet.
And in 1952, she went to Argentina and I stayed here in California. And --
